newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks end higher, led by Pudong.
newsitem.headline: China stocks end higher, led by Pudong.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended up on Friday, led by gains in Pudong shares in Shanghai, traders said.
But they said overseas institutions remained sidelined awaiting the release of the bulk of listed firms' 1996 results.
Shanghai's B share index rose 0.554 points, or 0.81 percent, to 69.099 on volume of 22.7 million shares worth $9.6 million.
Shenzhen's B index rose 0.94 points, or 0.61 percent, to 156.42 on turnover of HK$55.25 million.

Brokers said strong performances on Shanghai's A share market by Pudong shares -- companies involved in the development of the booming Pudong industrial zone outside Shanghai -- increased domestic buying in Pudong shares on the B share market in the afternoon session.
Pudong, located across the Huangpu River from the city's historic waterfront Bund, is Shanghai's premier development zone.

Shenzhen indices were pulled up by the Shanghai stock market's gains, brokers based in Shenzhen said, but they added that Shenzhen had less upward potential than Shanghai because of its already high price levels.
"Investors in Shenzhen were encouraged by Shanghai's gains and tried to catch up with the Shanghai market," said one broker. "But Shenzhen's B index is unlikely to rise sharply at such high levels."

On Shanghai's B share market, real estate developer Shanghai Wai Gaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development, the most active counter, was the star on a technical rebound, up $0.024, or 5.55 percent, to $0.456 on volume of 2.7 million shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development, another Pudong real estate firm, gained $0.032, or 3.77 percent, to $0.880 on volume of 1.9 million shares.
On Shenzhen's B share market, Shenzhen Petrochemical (Holdings) Co Ltd was the best performer, gaining HK$0.16, or 3.72 percent, to HK$4.46 with 292,820 shares changing hands.
Shanghai's A share index rose 23.350 points, or 2.07 percent, to 1,150.391 points on volume of 778.6 million shares worth 8.9 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index put on 79.074 points, or 2.76 percent, to 2,942.143 points.
Yunnan Baoshan Cement was the star on talk of institutional interest, surging 0.71 yuan, or 10.07 percent, to 7.76 yuan on volume of 2.9 million shares.
Shenzhen's A share index jumped 6.83 points, or 1.73 percent, to 402.15 on turnover of 7.00 billion yuan.
Jiamusi Paper Co Ltd, which listed 50 million A shares in Shenzhen on Monday, showed the strongest gains and rose to 12.37 yuan from an issue price of 4.70 yuan on volume of 30.6 million shares.
